title: Worksheet 6: Infinite Loops
directions: Read the paragraph below carefully. Then answer all questions using ONLY the information in the paragraph. Circle the letter of the best answer.
paragraph: An infinite loop is a loop that continues repeating forever, without ever stopping, usually because its stopping condition is written incorrectly or never actually becomes false while the program runs. Infinite loops are almost always a mistake rather than an intentional part of a program, since a program stuck in an infinite loop will typically stop responding to anything else, forcing a user to manually stop or restart the program to regain control. A common cause of an accidental infinite loop is forgetting to update the value that a while loop's condition depends on; for example, if a while loop is supposed to run only while a counter is less than 10, but the code inside the loop never actually increases that counter, the counter will remain at its starting value forever, and the condition "counter is less than 10" will never become false. Because for loops automatically manage their own counter as part of how they're built, they are generally somewhat less likely to accidentally become infinite loops compared to while loops, although it is still technically possible to write an infinite for loop under unusual circumstances.
